name: Tom Cotton
summary: Tom Cotton is a Republican U.S. senator from Arkansas and a hawkish conservative on national security, crime, immigration and China. He supports a strong military, harsh sentencing and the death penalty, reduced legal immigration, abortion limits and gun rights, and opposes socialism and Democratic proposals on policing and drugs.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Introduced a resolution condemning the "defund the police" movement and attacks Democrats for pursuing it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted for bills limiting it at 20 weeks, on taxpayer funding and on born-alive care; the sources show restrictions rather than a call to ban it in most cases.

central-planning.rationale: Says socialism inflicts brutality and poverty and that the Green New Deal's planning would be the envy of Soviet Russia.

death-penalty.rationale: Defends capital punishment for terrorists and mass murderers and condemned Biden's commutation of death sentences and the 9/11 plea deal, saying he strongly disagrees with the senator who wants such sentences commuted.

defeat-communism.rationale: Frames the economic contest with Communist China as one to fight rather than surrender and calls it the world's greatest threat, rather than seeking coexistence.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Presses for full funding of the US nuclear triad and sea-launched nuclear missile as the country's own deterrent against Russia and China.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Calls Israel the Jewish State and defends it as under siege and diplomatic assault, urging unconditional US backing.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Pressed Navy and Air Force nominees to fund the nuclear triad, including the nuclear sea-launched cruise missile, as a guaranteed second strike against Russia and China.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Attacked Gupta for her support of decriminalizing all drugs, and treats drug dealing as a crime to be punished harshly.

limit-guns.rationale: Attacked Garland and an ATF nominee for planning to weaken the Second Amendment and ban modern hunting rifles, so he opposes strict limits on gun ownership.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Introduced a bill giving traffickers who pass off fentanyl 20 years, and life or death-penalty eligibility with a prior felony record or a death, and says there can be no leniency for them.

military-force-beyond-defence.rationale: Defended Operation Epic Fury against Iran and the raid on Maduro as justified uses of force, and has urged military force to stop Iran getting nuclear weapons.

military-superiority.rationale: Warns that the US is surrendering its lead and eroding its military edge while enemies catch up, and calls for a bigger defense budget.

public-ownership.rationale: Opposes a socialist takeover of healthcare and denounces socialism as brutal and impoverishing.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Co-wrote the RAISE Act to cut legal immigration, ending the lottery and chain migration and replacing low-skilled with high-skilled entry, saying the current million a year hurts working-class Americans.

rehabilitation.rationale: Called the First Step Act the worst mistake of the Trump administration and says incarceration works and that mass incarceration is a myth.

restrict-technology-exports-to-rivals.rationale: Praises tightening export controls on sensitive technology to China and Huawei sanctions, and presses witnesses for stricter controls.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Voted yes on the 2023 resolution disapproving the Biden administration's student-loan cancellation (H.J.Res.45), which passed the Senate.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Calls section 702 of FISA a critical national security tool that stops terrorist attacks and defends it on the floor against Democratic opposition.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Voted nay on the 2015 amendment to reaffirm the prohibition on torture (H.R.1735), which passed 78-21.

voter-id.rationale: Urged passage of the SAVE America Act and defended photo ID for voting as common sense that most voters, including most Democrats, support.
